question: The price of 1 kg of carrot on Monday is ₹40. If it is increased by 5% and 3% on the next two consecutive days, then what is its price (in ₹) on Wednesday?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Percentage Increase = a + b + (a × b / 100)

Successive Increase = 5 + 3 + (5 × 3 / 100) = 8.15%

Price on Wednesday = 40 + (8.15% of 40)

⇒ 40 + 3.26 = 43.26

**∴ The correct answer is 43.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 ₹40 Monday 
• +5% ₹42 Tuesday 
• +3% ₹43.26 Wednesday 
 

Given:

Initial Price (Monday) = ₹40

Increase on Tuesday = 5%

Increase on Wednesday = 3%

Formula: Final Price = Initial Price × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

⇒ Price on Tuesday = 40 × (1 + 5/100)

⇒ Price on Tuesday = 40 × 1.05 = ₹42

⇒ Price on Wednesday = 42 × (1 + 3/100)

⇒ Price on Wednesday = 42 × 1.03

⇒ Price on Wednesday = ₹43.26

**∴ The correct answer is 43.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Multiplier Factor

An x% increase is equivalent to multiplying the initial value by (1 + x/100). For example, a 5% increase means multiplying by 1.05.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.
